en: Now begins the section on perception (saṃjñā).
Salutation to that Pāṇini, who, having received the traditional enumeration of phonemes from Maheśvara, proclaimed the entire science of grammar.
Salutations to that Pāṇini, by whom the speech of men was purified with the stainless waters of his words, and by whom the darkness born of ignorance was shattered. 2.
I bow to the triad of sages: Vararuci, the author of the Vākya; Patañjali, the author of the Bhāṣya; and Pāṇini, the author of the Sūtras. (3)
Having paid homage to the Three Sages and having reflected upon their teachings,
this *Vaiyākaraṇasiddhāntakaumudī* is composed.
"SK 00 AS 0-0-1" refers to the aphorisms of the followers of Maheśvara, which serve the purpose of establishing technical designations such as "aṇ" and so forth.
The final letter of these [groups] is [the marker]; in this *laṇ* sūtra, the vowel *a* is for the sake of pronunciation, as is the vowel *a* following the letter *ha*.
In the sūtra "hal" (Māṇḍūkya-sūtra-Saṃdarbha 14), the final letter shall be the *it*.
When the first [phoneme] is joined with the final *it*, it shall be the designation for itself and for those situated between them.
Thus, regarding the designation *hal*: in an original enunciation (*upadeśa*), the final consonant (*hal*) shall be termed *it*; "original enunciation" refers to the first utterance.
Then, once the technical designations such as *aṇ*, *ac*, and so forth are established, [the following applies]:
In the Upadeśa (the original enunciation), that which possesses a nasalized vowel shall be designated as *it*.
The followers of Pāṇini acknowledge the nasalization by convention (*pratijñānunāsikya*).
The letter *r*, when pronounced together with the vowel *a* situated in the *laṇ* sūtra, is the technical name for both *r* and *l*.
These [nasal stops] are not included in the *pratyāhāra* "it" (the *it* of *it-au*), because of the specific instruction in the rule beginning with "anunāsikaḥ";
for in this case, no operation conditioned by a vowel (*ac*) is observed when the letter *k* follows.
Those [groups] formed by the sūtra "the first [vowel] with the last" (Pāṇini 1.1.71) are designated by the term *pratyāhāra*.
The vowels *u*, *ū*, and *ū3*—
that which has these as its "time" (*kāla*) like the time itself— is designated by the terms short (*hrasva*), long (*dīrgha*), and protracted (*pluta*) respectively;
each of these is further threefold according to the distinctions of acute (*udātta*) and the other accents.
In the places of articulation such as the palate and others which possess distinct parts, that sound produced in the upper part shall be designated as *udātta* (high-pitched).
Those who [come]... (SK 6; AS 1.2.30)
Clearly directed hitherward.
(SK 7)
That vowel (*ac*) in which both the acute (*udātta*) and grave (*anudātta*) pitches are combined shall be designated as circumflex (*svarita*).
(SK 8)
In the rule AS 1.2.32, the mention of "short" (hrasva) is not restrictive; it should be understood that the first half of a svarita vowel is udātta.
The second half [of the vowel], however, is by default *anudātta* (unaccented);
its audible manifestation is clearly as such when followed by an *udātta* or *svarita*,
whereas in other cases, an *udātta*-like resonance is well-known in the *Prātiśākhya*.
Where are your horses,
those which draw the chariots with a hundred wheels? For yesterday they were yoked.
In cases such as these, there is the *anudātta* (low-pitched) accent;
in cases such as *agnim īḷe*, there is the perception of the *udātta* (high-pitched) accent.
Although this [vowel] is of nine kinds, each is further twofold by virtue of being either nasalized (*anunāsika*) or non-nasalized (*ananunāsika*).
A phoneme uttered with the nose together with the mouth shall be designated as *anunāsika* (nasalized).
Thus, for these vowels—a, i, u, ṛ—there are eighteen varieties each;
for the vowel *lṛ*, there are twelve, because it lacks a long form;
and for the diphthongs (*e*, *ai*, *o*, *au*), there are also twelve, because they lack short forms.

That pair consisting of the place of articulation, such as the palate, and the internal effort— whatever has the same [place and effort] as another shall have the technical designation *savarṇa* (homogeneous) with respect to one another.
The throat is the place of articulation for the vowels *a*, *u*, *ṛ*, and the visarga; the palate for *i*, *cu*, *ya*, and *śa*; and the head for *ṛ*, *ṭu*, *ra*, and *ṣa*.

The teeth are the points of articulation for *lṛ*, *t*, *th*, *d*, *dh*, *s*, and *ṣ*; the lips are those for *u*, *ū*, *p*, *ph*, and the *upadhmānīya*; and the nose is that for *ñ*, *m*, *ṅ*, *ṇ*, and *n*.
The *e* and *ai* sounds have their place of articulation in the throat and palate;
the *o* and *au* sounds have their place in the throat and lips;
and the *va* sound has its place in the teeth and lips.
The places of articulation are the root of the tongue for the jihvāmūlīya and the nose for the anusvāra.
Effort (*yatna*) is twofold: internal and external.
The former is fourfold, due to the distinctions of *spṛṣṭa* (contacted), *īṣatspṛṣṭa* (slightly contacted), *vivṛta* (open), and *saṃvṛta* (contracted).
Among these, the effort of *spṛṣṭa* belongs to the *sparśa* (stop) consonants.
The semi-vowels (*antasthā*) are slightly contacted;
the sibilants (*ūṣman*) and vowels are widely opened;
and the vowel *a* is contracted when it is short.
However, in the state of grammatical derivation (*prakriyā-daśā*), this [substitution] is indeed fully manifested;
and this has been indicated by the author of the Sūtras as follows:
Having restated what was explained in SK 11 (AS 8.4.68), the *saṃvṛta* [vowel] is prescribed by this [rule].
And because this [unmanifested state] is not established with respect to the entire *Aṣṭādhyāyī*, it indeed possesses the quality of being "opened" from the perspective of the treatise;
and thus the Sūtra (SK 12) states: [The unmanifested is characterized by the absence of these qualities].
This is a governing heading (adhikāra).

By this, the Tripādī is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) with respect to the first seven chapters and a quarter; furthermore, within the Tripādī itself, a subsequent rule is to be regarded as non-existent with respect to a preceding one.

The external effort (*bāhyaprayatna*), however, is of eleven kinds: *vivāra* (openness), *saṃvāra* (closure), *śvāsa* (breath), *nāda* (sound), *ghoṣa* (voiced), *aghoṣa* (unvoiced), *alpaprāṇa* (unaspirated), *mahāprāṇa* (aspirated), *udātta* (high-pitched), *anudātta* (low-pitched), and *svarita* (circumflex). Among these, the *yamās* of the *khay* series, the *khay* letters themselves, *k*, *p*, *visarga*, and the *śar* letters—these have breath as their external effort (*śvāsānupradāna*), are unvoiced (*aghoṣa*), and involve openness (*vivṛṇvate*).

Others, however, hold that voiced consonants are produced in the throat and are characterized by a closed articulation; among them, the odd-numbered members of the classes (*varga*), the semivowels (*yama*), and the *yaṇ* sounds are considered to have little breath-force (*alpāsava*).
In the Prātiśākhya, it is well known that when the fifth letter follows the first four letters of a class, there arises in between a sound called *yama*, which resembles its predecessor.
The two women cooked the fire.
In the word *ghghnantīti*, there are *yamas* (nasalized counterparts) similar to the letters *ka, kha, ga,* and *gha* respectively following them.

Among these, the first and second letters of the classes (*vargas*), the three sibilants (*śa, ṣa, sa*), as well as their corresponding *yamas*, the *jihvāmūlīya*, the *upadhmānīya*, the *visarga*, and *śa, ṣa, sa*—these possess wide opening (*vivāra*), aspiration (*śvāsa*), and lack of voicing (*aghoṣa*).
For all others, however, there is narrow opening (*saṃvāra*), resonance (*nāda*), and voicing (*ghoṣa*).
The first, third, and fifth letters of each varga, as well as *ya*, *ra*, *la*, and *va*—along with the first and third *yamas*—are "unaspirated" (*alpaprāṇa*);
the others are "aspirated" (*mahāprāṇa*). This is the meaning.

Furthermore, although these external efforts (*bāhyaprayatna*) are not utilized in the definition of "homogeneity" (*savarṇasaṃjñā*), it should be understood that they will be employed in the examination of "closest similarity" (*āntaratamya*).
The consonants beginning with *ka* and ending with *ma* are the *sparśa*s; *ya*, *ra*, *la*, and *va* are the *antasthā*s; and *śa*, *ṣa*, *sa*, and *ha* are the *ūṣman*s.
Vowels are *a*, *i*, *u*, *ṛ*, *ḷ*, *e*, *o*, and *ai*.
The *ka* and *pa* groups [of consonants] are those beginning with *k* and *p*. Before these, there are the *jihvāmūlīya* and *upadhmānīya*, which resemble the half-visarga (*ḥ*).
The *anusvāra* and *visarga* follow vowels as *aṃ* and *aḥ*.
Thus concludes the analysis of place and effort.
It should be stated that *ṛ* and *ḷ* are mutually homogeneous (*sāvarṇya*).
Since mutual homogeneity would otherwise result between *a* and *ha*, *i* and *śa*, *ṛ* and *ṣa*, and *ḷ* and *sa*:
An *ac* vowel accompanied by its *ā-kāra* (long vowel) and a *hal* consonant— these two are not *savarṇa* (homogeneous) with one another.

Therefore, in the case of the word *dadhi* followed by *iti*, *harati*, *śītalam*, *ṣaṣṭham*, or *sāndram*, the substitution of *yaṇ* and so forth does not occur; otherwise, by the force of the *grahaṇaka-śāstra*, even the letters *h* and others would possess the status of vowels (*actva*), just as the long vowels and others do. For instance: [The rule: "When *eC* follows *eC*, *aiC* is substituted [for both]. (Pāṇini 6.1.90) [The rule: "When *oT* follows *oT*, *auT* is substituted [for both]. (Pāṇini 6.1.91) [The rule: "When *iK* follows *iK*, *yaṇ* is substituted [for both]. (Pāṇini 6.1.77) In these rules, the *eC*, *oT*, and *iK* are taught as being included within the term *eC*. Now, if it were the case that the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* applied here as well—namely, that "the *eC* mentioned in this rule includes the letters *e*, *ai*, *o*, and *au*"—then the *h* in *hotṛ* would also be included in the *eC* category. Consequently, when *hotṛ* is followed by *iti*, the *yaṇ* substitution would apply, resulting in the form *hotṛti*. However, since the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* does not apply here, the *h* is not considered an *eC*, and thus the *yaṇ* substitution does not take place. Furthermore, if the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* were to apply here, then in the case of *hotṛ + ojaḥ*, the *o* of *ojaḥ* would also be included in the *oT* category. Consequently, when *hotṛ* is followed by *ojaḥ*, the *auT* substitution would apply, resulting in the form *hotraujaḥ*. However, since the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* does not apply here, the *o* is not considered an *oT*, and thus the *auT* substitution does not take place. Moreover, if the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* were to apply here, then in the case of *hotṛ + indraḥ*, the *i* of *indraḥ* would also be included in the *iK* category. Consequently, when *hotṛ* is followed by *indraḥ*, the *yaṇ* substitution would apply, resulting in the form *hotryendraḥ*. However, since the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* does not apply here, the *i* is not considered an *iK*, and thus the *yaṇ* substitution does not take place. Therefore, the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* does not apply to the *eC*, *oT*, and *iK* mentioned in these rules. This is because the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* is established based on the principle that "when a grammatical operation is prescribed for a specific letter, that letter is understood to include its own class," whereas in these cases, no such operation is prescribed for the individual letters *e*, *ai*, *o*, or *au*. Thus, the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* does not extend to them. However, in the case of the *iK* mentioned in the rule "When *iK* follows *iK*, *yaṇ* is substituted" (Pāṇini 6.1.77), the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* does indeed apply. This is because the *yaṇ* substitution is specifically prescribed for the *iK* mentioned in that rule. Therefore, the *i* in *hotṛ* is included in the *iK* category, and when *hotṛ* is followed by *indram*, the *yaṇ* substitution applies, resulting in the form *hotṛndram*. Thus, the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* applies to the *iK* mentioned in the rule "When *iK* follows *iK*, *yaṇ* is substituted" (Pāṇini 6.1.77), but it does not apply to the *eC*, *oT*, or *iK* mentioned in the rules "When *eC* follows *eC*, *aiC* is substituted" (Pāṇini 6.1.90), "When *oT* follows *oT*, *auT* is substituted" (Pāṇini 6.1.91), or "When *iK* follows *iK*, *yaṇ* is substituted" (Pāṇini 6.1.77) [in the sense of including other letters]. This is because the former is a rule prescribing an operation for the *iK* itself, while the latter are rules where no operation is prescribed for the individual letters *e*, *ai*, *o*, or *au*. Consequently, the *grahaṇaka-śāstra* does not apply to those letters. That which is understood or enjoined is a *pratyaya* (suffix).
An *aṇ* and an *uc* that are not themselves being prescribed shall be the technical term (*saṃjñā*) for their homogeneous sounds (*savarṇa*).
Here, the *aṇ* is defined by the subsequent *ṇakāra*, while *ku*, *cu*, *ṭu*, *tu*, and *pu* are the *udit* (those followed by *t*).
Thus,
"a" is the designation for eighteen [phonemes],
and likewise for "i" and "u."
The vowel *ṛ* is [the substitute] for thirty;
likewise, *lṛ* is also [the substitute] for twelve *eṅ* vowels.
Furthermore, there is no mutual homogeneity (*sāvarṇya*) between *e* and *ai*, or *o* and *au*, because of the force of the formulation of the rule *ai-au-jit*. Therefore,
one should not raise the objection that the technical designation (*saṃjñā*) would apply to all twenty-four vowels, including *e* and *ai*.

Although the prohibition "nājjhalau" (Pāṇini 1.1.10) applies only to those vowels and consonants included in the *akṣarasamāmnāya* (the traditional list of phonemes), nevertheless, the vowel *ā* is not a *savarṇa* (homogeneous) of the letter *h*, because the vowel *ā* is also [implicitly] included therein.
Consequently, in the word *viśvapābhiḥ*, the substitution of *ḍha* for *ha* by the rule "ho ḍhaḥ" (Pāṇini 8.2.31) does not occur.

The *y*, *v*, and *l* sounds are each twofold, distinguished by being nasal (*anunāsika*) or non-nasal (*ananunāsika*); therefore, those which are non-nasal serve as the designations for each respective pair. (SK 15)
That which follows *taḥ* (the letter *t*), as well as *taḥ* itself when being uttered after [another sound], shall be the designation for that which has the same duration;
by this rule, *at*, *it*, *ut*, and so forth, are the designations for the six [vowels].
"Ṛt" [is the name] of the twelve [syllables],
according to the Sāṃkhyakārikā 16 and the *Abhidharmasamuccaya* 1.1.1.
The term *ādaic* shall be designated as *vṛddhi*.
(SK 17; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.2)
The vowels *a*, *e*, and *o* shall be designated as *guṇa*.
(SK 18; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.2)
Verbal roots beginning with *bhū* that denote action shall be designated as *dhātu*.
(SK 19; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.3.1–4.56)
With reference to this,
[it is said] in Sāṃkhyakārikā 20 and Yogasūtra 1.4–57.
Particles such as *ca* and others, when devoid of substantive meaning (*adravyārtha*), shall be designated as *nipāta*.
(SK 21; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.4.58)
Likewise, particles such as *pra* and others do not denote substances; [this is stated] in Pāṇini’s Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.4.58–59.

SK 23 / AS 1.4.58–60: The words beginning with *pra*, when used in connection with an action (*kriyāyoga*), shall bear the technical designations of *upasarga* (preverb) and *gati* (indeclinable particle).
*pra*, *parā*, *apa*, *sam*, *anu*, *ava*, *nis*, *nir*, *dur*, *duṣ*, *vi*, *āṅ*, *ni*, *adhi*, *api*, *ati*, *su*, *ud*, *abhi*, *prati*, and *pari*—these are the *upasargas*.
The designation "vibhāṣā" (optionality) shall apply to both negation and alternative. (SK 25; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.44)
In the science of grammar, a word's own form is the designatum (saṃjñin), except for those words that are themselves technical terms (saṃjñā). (Pāṇini 1.1.68)

A qualifier [applied] to that which ends in a suffix shall be a designation for itself and for its own form; however, there is a prohibition in the case of rules prescribing compounds and suffixes. (Vārttika).
This applies with the exception of those rules involving *ugit* suffixes and the mention of specific phonemes (*varṇa*). (Vārttika).
The absence of phonemes (varṇa) shall be termed *avasāna* (pause).
The excessive proximity of phonemes (varṇa) shall be designated as *saṃhitā*.
That which ends in a nominal suffix (subanta) and that which ends in a verbal suffix (tiṅanta) shall be designated as a "word" (pada).
Consonants not separated by vowels shall be termed *saṃyoga* (conjunction).
Sāṃkhyakārikā 31; Āgamaśāstra 1.4.10–10; Sāṃkhyakārikā 32.
In the presence of a following conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*), a short vowel shall be designated as heavy (*guru*). (SK 33)
"And a long [vowel] shall have the designation 'heavy'";
thus ends the section on technical designations (*saṃjñā*).
Now begins the section on technical definitions (paribhāṣāprakaraṇa).
Wherever the terms *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* are used to enjoin *guṇa* or *vṛddhi*, the word *ikaḥ* in the genitive case stands as a governing term [supplying the referent]. (SK 35; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.28)
Where the terms *hrasva* (short), *dīrgha* (long), and *pluta* (protracted) are prescribed, the word *acaḥ* (of a vowel), ending in the genitive case, is supplied [from the previous rule].
(SK 36; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.2.46)
The *ṭit* and *kit* suffixes are, respectively, the initial and final constituents of that [element] to which they are said to belong.
(SK 37; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.47)

The word "ca" (and) is used here in the sense of selection (*nirdhāraṇa*), [indicating] a genitive case; among the vowels (*acām*), that which is the last—after that [vowel], only its own final constituent (*antāvayava*) shall be a *mit* [augment].
A genitive case ending whose specific relation is not determined should be understood as denoting "in place of" (sthāne-yoga);
and "place" (sthāna) means "occasion" (prasaṅga).
When there is an occasion for substitution, that which is most similar [to the original] shall be the substitute.
Where there is a conflict between various types of proximity (*āntarya*), proximity by location (*sthāna*) is stronger.

An operation prescribed by a rule employing the seventh case (saptamī) should be understood as applying to that which precedes it and is not separated from it by another phoneme. (SK 41; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.67)

An operation performed by means of a designation in the fifth case (pañcamī) should be understood as applying to a subsequent element that is not separated by another phoneme. (SK 42 / Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.52)
An *ādeśa* (substitute) shall take the place of the final *al* (vowel or consonant) of that which is designated by the genitive case.
(Pāṇini 1.1.52)
This [rule] also serves as an exception (apavāda) to the rule "this too shall belong to the last [of all]" (SK 45).
SK 44.
That which is prescribed for a subsequent element should be understood as applying to its initial [element];
this is an exception (apavāda) to the rule "alo'ntyasya" (Pāṇini 1.1.52).
SK 45 AS 1-1-55 is clear.
This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule *alo'ntyasya* (Pāṇini 1.1.52).
In cases such as *aṣṭābhya auś* (Pāṇini 7.1.21), even the rule *deḥ parasya* (Pāṇini 1.1.54) is superseded by this [present rule] because of its higher status (*paratva*). (SK 46)
AS 1.3.11: It should be understood that the word-form (*śabdasvarūpa*) marked with the *svarita* accent is the subject under discussion;
furthermore, among rules that are *para*, *nitya*, *antaraṅga*, and *apavāda*, each subsequent one is stronger than the preceding.
The meaning is: "That which is external is not established when [the internal operation has already taken effect];
the followers of Pāṇini do not perform an operation caused by a cause that they perceive to be on the verge of destruction. This is known as the *akṛtavyūha-paribhāṣā*.
Thus ends the section on technical rules (paribhāṣā); now begins the section on vowel-sandhi (acsandhi). SK 47
According to Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.77, *yaṇ* shall substitute for *ik* in the domain of *saṃhitā* when followed by a vowel;
thus, in the case of "sudhī upāsyaḥ," the following state is established: [sudhy upāsyaḥ].
Due to the position [of the letters] and because of proximity, the letter *y* replaces the vowel *ī* in the word *sudhī*,
resulting in the form *sudhy upāsya*. (SK 48)
According to AS 8.4.47,
"A consonant following a vowel may optionally be doubled, except when followed by a vowel," there is doubling of the letter *dh*.
An *ādeśa* (substitute) shall be treated like the *sthānin* (original element), except in a rule that depends on the phonemes (*al*) of the *sthānin*.

In this context, one should not suspect a prohibition of doubling by rule P. 6.1.48 (*anaci ca*), based on the assumption that the letter *ya* possesses the status of a vowel (*actva*) through its status as a *sthānin*; for that [prohibition] is barred by the restriction "not in the case of an operation concerning an *al*" (P.

This [sūtra] is for the purpose of excluding [the application of] *alvidhi*: "A substitute (*ajādeśa*) caused by something else shall be treated like the original (*sthānivadbhavati*) when an operation (*vidhi*) is to be performed regarding that which was previously seen as preceding the original sound (*sthānī*). Thus, since the status of being a substitute for the *yaṇ* [vowels] would have been obtained [by the previous rule], [this sūtra is stated].

When an operation is to be performed on the final element of a word, or on [elements such as] reduplication, a substitute for *ac* (a vowel) caused by a subsequent element is not treated as *sthānivadbhūta*.
Thus ends the prohibition of the status of being like the original (sthānivadbhāva) [according to Pāṇini 1.1.56],
[as stated in] SK 52 and AS 8.4.53.

The Bhāṣya states, "The agent [of the action] is either equal [to the object], or some [hold that there is] elision. "You will come tomorrow;

however, when there is the qualification "from what is not *apluta*," by the force of that [qualification], there is no invalidity (*asiddhatva*). But the long vowel marker (*tapara*) has no such force, because its purpose is fulfilled by the exclusion of long vowels.

who has gone beyond the past.
In this case (SK 223, AS 1-1-30), the status of being a pronoun (sarvanāmatā) would not apply.
Even in a sentence expressing the meaning of a compound such as *māsapūrvāya* (preceded by a month), [the suffix] is not applied to *māsena pūrvāya*.
In a *dvandva* compound, the technical designation (*saṃjñā*) previously mentioned does not apply.
This prohibition applies to the aggregate of the classes (varṇa), stages of life (āśrama), and others, but not to their individual components;
nor, in this way, does the rule for suffixing [the augment] *suṭ* apply by means of the principle of "ending-in-that" (*tadantavidhi*).
Because it has been explained that *suṭ* is the augment applied to the genitive plural ending *ām* when it follows a pronominal stem (*sarvanāman*).

When the grammatical operation known as *śībhāva*— which has *jas* as its basis— is to be applied, the previously mentioned technical designation (*saṃjñā*) for the *dvandva* compound may optionally apply; thus,
one says either *varṇāśrametaraḥ* or *varṇāśrametarāḥ*.
It has been stated that the option (*vibhāṣā*) applies only with respect to the substitution of *śī* [for *asti*]; therefore, there is no *akac* suffix,
but rather only the *kapratyaya* suffix, as in the case of *varṇāśrametarakāḥ*.
These [pronominal stems] may optionally be designated as "already-stated" (ukta-saṃjñā) with respect to the operation of the suffix *jas*.
In the first [case], the first [forms] apply; the remainder is like that of Rāma.
From that [set of three], the last three conditions are to be taken; in the pair [of causes], the two [conditions] are to be taken.
The rest is like Rāma; he is not one who bows, nor are these [others] those who bow.
The remainder is as in all cases; in the section on *vibhāṣā*, there is an addition (*upasaṅkhyāna*) to the rule for the *ṅit* suffixes regarding the ordinal *tīya*:
[the form] *dvitīyasmai*.
"For the second case ending," and so forth;
likewise for the third case ending,
[the suffix] does not apply here because of the mention of "meaningful" (*arthavat*) elements.
The soul is of a sharp nature.

In the context of rules concerning words and their constituents (*pada* and *aṅga*), the word *jarā* may optionally be replaced by *jaras* before vowel-initial case endings; this applies both to the word itself and to that which ends in it.

Since it consists of more than one *al* (phoneme), the rule for universal substitution (*sarvādeśa*) would apply; however, substitutions occur only for that which is explicitly mentioned [in the rule],
and because that which has undergone a partial modification is not considered different from the original, the word *jara* becomes *jaras*.
In the case of *nirjarasau* and *nirjarasaḥ*,
the form *jaras* replaces *in* and the other suffixes because it is subsequent [in the order of rules].
O ageless one, you who are ageless, for the sake of the ageless ones.

In the case of [the suffix] *bhyas* and before consonant-initial [suffixes], the author of the *Vṛtti* states that, like *rāma*, some hold that by means of a prior counter-exception (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*), after *in* and *āt* have been applied, one assumes the non-eternality (*anityatva*) of the *saṃnipātaparibhāṣā*; thus, having applied *jaras*, the forms *nirjarasina* and *nirjarasāt* arise, but not *nirjarasā* and *nirjarasaḥ*.
Likewise, for the case ending *bhis*, he mentions another form: *nirjarasaiḥ*.
And those who follow that [view] have accepted the form *nirjarasya* in the singular genitive case;
however, this contradicts the Bhāṣya (SK 228).

For *pāda*, *danta*, *nāsikā*, *māsa*, *hṛdaya*, *niśā*, *asṛj*, *yūṣ*, *doṣ*, *yakṛt*, *śakṛt*, *udaka*, and *āsya*, the substitutes beginning with *pad* shall optionally occur before suffixes beginning with *śas*.
As for what was stated in the Kāśikā—that there is an *āsanna* substitute for the word *āsana*—that is an error.
One foot,
two feet,
many feet.
A foot,
two feet,
or many feet.
"Foot with foot," "foot by foot," and so forth.
SK 229 AS 1.1.43: *suṭ* is a pratyāhāra.
The five case endings beginning with *su* shall bear the technical designation *sarvanāmasthāna* when they do not belong to a neuter noun. (SK 230; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.1.42–43)

When followed by suffixes beginning with *sva* (i.e., case endings) that are not *sarvanāmasthāna*, and up to those ending in the *kap* suffix, the preceding element shall be designated as a *pada*. (Pāṇini 1.4.17–18)

When followed by suffixes beginning with *ka* (excluding those beginning with vowels), as well as by suffixes beginning with *sva* that are not *sarvanāmasthāna*, the preceding element shall receive the designation *bha*.
(SK 232; Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.4.18)
From this point forward, up until the rule *kaḍārāḥ karmadhāraye*, only one designation (saṃjñā) should be understood for each [term],
whichever is subsequent and non-redundant (*anavakāśā*).
Consequently, when an *ac* vowel follows suffixes such as *śas*, there is only the designation *bha*, and not the designation *pada*.
Therefore, there is no substitution of the voiced unaspirated stop (*jaś*) for *d* in *dataḥ* and *datā*.
The substitution of *jaś* [for *c* and *ch*] occurs after [the sounds] *da* and *dha*, and so forth; [the word] *māsaḥ*.
When *mās* undergoes *rutva* and *yatva*, there is the elision of *y*; thus,
*mābhyām*.
*mābhiḥ* and so forth (Pāṇini 6.4.129).
This is a governing rule (adhikāra).

There shall be elision (*lopa*) of the *akāra* of that *an* which is a member of a word-base (*aṅgāvayava*), provided it is not followed by a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix or by a suffix beginning with *ya* or *su*. (Pāṇini 6.4.134)
The *n* following the single-consonant sounds *r* and *ṣ* shall become *ṇ*; as in *yūṣṇaḥ* and *yūṣṇā*.

Even according to the view that there is the status of being a *sthānin* (*sthānivadbhāva*) with respect to a preceding rule in the case of an operation, the substitution of *ṇ* occurs here by the rule *aḍvyavāye* itself; however, the exception "it is not like the *sthānin* with regard to what precedes" does not apply here (or rather, its fault is avoided) because of the prohibition: "there is no [application of] *pūrvatrāsiddham* in the cases of the elision of the first member of a conjunct consonant (*saṃyogādilopa*), the substitution of *l*, and the substitution of *ṇ*."
In the sūtras "neti" (SK 236) and "prātipadika" (AS 8.2.7), the words are those in which the genitive case ending has been elided.
There shall be elision of the *n* at the end of that word which is designated as a nominal stem (*prātipadika*).
Because the elision of *n* is treated as non-existent (*asiddha*), the lengthening, the substitution of *e*, and the substitution of *ai* do not occur;
thus, [the form is] *yūṣabhyām*.
"From the juices, for the juices," and so forth (SK 237).

When followed by the locative singular ending *ṅi* (as) or the nominative/accusative dual ending *śi*, the *a* of an *an* which is a constituent part of a stem (*aṅga*)— provided that this *an* is not followed by an *asarvanāmasthāna* suffix beginning with *y* or *j*, or by a *svādi* (case-ending from *su* onwards)— is optionally elided when the word ends in *yūṣan*.

In the rule *yūṣan-māṃsa-pārśva-śāka-yavābhyas chaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.4.91), the inclusion of the term *prabhṛti* ("and so forth") serves to indicate that the list is illustrative (*prakāra*). This is analogous to the case of *rāma-vat* in the rule *paddanno-māsan-yūṣan-doṣan-yakkan-khann-añ-nin-aś-ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.63).
And likewise, even when the case-ending *auṅ* is replaced by *śī*, the substitution of *doṣan* is illustrated in the Bhāṣya with the example *kakuddoṣaṇī*;
by this, the following [definitions] are consistent: "the word *pad* [is used] for 'foot' in the non-feminine," and "the words *svānta*, *hrat*, *mānasa*, and *manas* [denote] the mind."

And regarding the statement "they spoke to the breath in the mouth" (*āsanyaṃ prāṇam ūcuḥ*), the term *āsanya* means "situated in the mouth" (*āsye bhavaḥ*); furthermore, the neuter gender of the word *doṣ* is also established by this very commentary.
By this, it is consistent that "daksinam dornisacara" (the night-stalker with his right arm) is used;

for "bhuja," "bāhu," and "praveshta" are synonyms for "doḥ" (arm), and by virtue of their association, the masculine gender is also employed. Furthermore, the fault [of the opponent] is that he attributes such a state to him; thus, "dvyahnaḥ" means that which occurs during two days.
In the locative case (ṅi), for a word preceded by a numeral or the like, the substitution of *ahan* for *ahar* may optionally take place.
Every two days;
on every second day.
vigamahar-vyahnaḥ, vyahe, vyaheṣu; vyahe, vyaheṣu.
vyahne, ahnaḥ, sāyaḥ, sāyāhnaḥ,
sāyāhni.
*sāyāhani* and *sāyāhne* are examples of words ending in the vowel -a.
viśvapāḥ (SK 239; AS 6.1.105)
When *jas* follows a long vowel, and when *ic* follows, the single long substitute (pūrvasavarṇadīrgha) for the first two cases shall not occur; instead,
there is *vṛddhi*, as in *viśvapau*.
Regarding the *savarṇadīrgha* (long vowel resulting from the coalescence of similar vowels):

although in the case of *viśvapau* [the dual nominative/accusative] the desired form is already established by Pāṇini 6.1.102 (*auṅ āpaḥ*), and in the case of *jasi* there is no harm even if the *pūrvasavarṇadīrgha* occurs, nevertheless, for the sake of forms such as *gaurī-au* and *gaurī-as*, this rule is appropriately cited here as well.
When a stem ending in a verbal root that ends in the vowel *ā* is a *bha* member, its final phoneme shall be elided.
"Of the final [element], [the substitute takes the place of] that which follows *al*" (Pāṇini 1.1.52). Thus,
from *viśvapāḥ* [we derive] *viśvapābhyām*, and so forth.
In this way, [the words] *śaṅkha*, *ādhmāta*, and so forth—
what [is the result] from the verbal root? *hāhān*.
*ṭā*: *savarṇadīrgha* (long vowel substitution with a homogeneous vowel) → *hāhā*; *ṅe*: *vṛddhi* (vṛddhi strengthening) → *hāhe*.
In the case of *hāhā* followed by the endings *ṅasi*, *ṅas*, or *ṅi*, there is a long vowel:
*hāhāḥ*.
osi, vṛddhiḥ, hāhauḥ, ṅau, ādguṇaḥ.
In *hāhe śeṣam* and *viśvapāvāt*,
there is the elision of the vowel *ā* even after a non-root [suffix], due to the division of the rule (*yogavibhāga*).
The suffixes *kttva* and *śna* end in the vowel *a*.
The word *hari* takes the *pūrvasavarṇa* substitute in the first two [cases]. *Harī*.
A guna substitute shall occur for a stem ending in a short vowel when followed by the suffix *jasi*;
[thus,] *harayaḥ*.
In the vocative case, a short vowel shall take its corresponding guṇa substitute.
By the rule "eṅhrasvāt saṃbuddheḥ" (Pāṇini 6.1.69), there is elision of the vocative case ending:
"he hare," "harim."
The two tawny ones.
SK 243
AS 1.4.7: Short *i* and *u*, not having the designation *anadī*, along with what ends in them—excluding those termed *sakhi*—shall have the designation *ghisamjñā*.
What is the purpose of the word "the rest" (*śeṣa*)?

The reality is that, although [the desired result] is established by the governing rule *ekasaṃjñā* (only one technical designation applies), the mention of the word *śeṣa* (remainder) is for the sake of clarity; [the question is:
why [are they] short?
O Vātapramyā,
what is this for you,
O mother?
After the suffix *ghi*, the substitute *nā* shall take the place of the following *aṅ* (genitive case ending), except in the feminine.
The designation *ṭā* for the [instrumental singular] ending *ā* belongs to the Easterners; [why is it said] "not in the feminine," as in *hariṇā*?
By means of cognition (matyā) [one attains the goal];
this is according to *Sāṃkhyakārikā* 245 and *Yogasūtra* 7.3.111.
There should be *guṇa* substitution for that which is designated as *gh*, before a *ṅit* case-ending (*sup*); [as in] *haraye*.
Why [is it said] "of *ghi*"?
In the case of a *sakhi* [stem] followed by a *ṅit* [suffix], as in *haribhyām*?
In the case of *supi*, what [is the result] when *guṇa* has been applied by [Pāṇini 1.1.3] "gher ṅiti"?
When *ṅasi* or *ṅas* follows, the single substitute for the preceding vowel (*eṅ*) and the following *at* shall be the form of the preceding vowel.
of Hari,
of two Haris,
of many Haris (horses)
After *i* and *u*, the *ṅi* case-ending shall be replaced by *auṭ*, and for a stem ending in *gh*, the final vowel shall be replaced by *a*.
He takes from two tawny ones among the tawny ones.
In this way, [the planets] Śrīpati, Agni, Ravi, Kavi, and so forth [are established].

In place of the member *sakhi*, there shall be the substitute *anaṅ* when followed by the nominative singular suffix *su* that is not a vocative; furthermore, this substitute is marked with the indicatory letter *ṅ*. (SK 249) This is the final substitution.
The letter preceding the final consonant (hal) shall be designated as the *upadhā*.
A long vowel shall not be substituted for the penultimate (upadhā) of that which ends in *n*, when followed by a *sarvanāmasthāna* case-ending other than the vocative singular.
A single-consonant suffix (apratyaya) which consists of only one phoneme shall be designated as *apṛkta*.

After a word ending in a consonant (*hal*), or after one ending in a long *ṅī* or *āp*, the uncombined (*apṛkta*) consonant *s* of the nominative (*su*) and accusative plural (*tis*) suffixes is elided. Why [mention] "after consonants, *ṅī*, and *āp" (*halṅyābbhyaḥ*)?
Is *grāmaṇīḥ* [the example] for *dīrghāt*, and *niṣkauśāmbiḥ* [the example] for *kim*?
Why did Atikhaṭva, crying out "sutisī," break it?
Because of the inclusion of *sip* as it occurs in association with *ti*, there is no inclusion of *sic*;
[the word] "apṛkta" [is used]— for example,
as in *bibharti*.
What did the first consonant split at the beginning?
The elision of *n* in the word *rājā* would not occur because the elision of the final consonant of a conjunct (*saṃyogāntalopa*) is considered non-existent (*asiddha*), as in the case of *sakhā*.
O friend!
After the word *sakhi*, when followed by a case-ending that is not the vocative singular, it is treated as having the augment *ṇit* (i.e., it takes the *guṇa* strengthening).
(SK 254; Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.93)
When a suffix beginning with *ṇ* or *ñ* follows, there shall be vṛddhi of the final vowel of a stem ending in a vowel; [e.g.,] *sakhāyau*, *sakhāyaḥ*.
In the case of *sakhāyam* and *sakhāyau*, because they lack the designation *ghisamjñā*, that grammatical operation [of shortening] does not apply.
A friend for a friend.
After the words *sakhi* and *pati*, when they have undergone the substitution of *yaṇ* [for the *i*], the vowel *a* of the case endings *ṅasi* and *ṅas* is replaced by *u*;
thus, [the forms] *sakhyuḥ* [and *patyuḥ* are obtained].
After *i* and *u*, the ending *ṅe* becomes *au*.
The recurrence of the term "ukāra" (the vowel *u*) is for the sake of what follows; in the sense of "friend," the remainder is like that of *hari*.
A good friend, *śobhanaḥ sakhā*; two good friends, *susakhāyau*; many good friends, *susakhāyaḥ*.

Because the status of being a stem (*aṅga*) applies to the entire complex, the operations of *anaṅ* (the substitution of *anaṅ* for the final vowel of the neuter *sakhi*) and *niṅtvabhāva* (the absence of the feminine suffix *niṅ*) also apply to the end of that complex; however,
since the whole does not possess the form of the word *sakhi*, the prohibition in *asakhi* (Pāṇini 1.4.7) does not apply, and thus the designation *ghisamjñā* is established for *susakhi*.
In *susakheḥ*,

when the guṇa substitution has been applied to the case endings *ṅasi* and *ṅas*, the substitution of *utva* (the replacement of *i* by *u*) does not occur because the condition of having undergone the *yaṇ* substitution is absent; this is according to Pāṇini 6.4.145 (*khyatyāt*).
Regarding "susakha" and so forth: in the analysis of the compound, it means one whose friend is an *atisakha*— that is, an exceedingly excellent friend— or a *paramasakha*, a supreme friend.
In forms such as *paramasakhā* and *paramasakhāyau*, even when the terms are used in a secondary (gauṇa) sense, the rules for the substitution of *anaṅ* and the designation *ṇit* still apply.
*atisakhi*, having transcended the *sakhi* [limit],
does not take the suffix *ṭac*— as in *harivat*— because the rule regarding gender-distinction (*liṅgaviśiṣṭaparibhāṣā*) is not universally applicable (*anitya*).
In this case, the [substitutions] *anaṅ* and *ṅit* do not occur; for, by the rule *go-striyoḥ* (Pāṇini 1.2.48), the word *sakhi* is treated as having a short vowel (*hrasva*),
and between that which is derived through a grammatical rule (*lākṣaṇika*) and that which is explicitly stated (*pratipadokta*), only the explicitly stated form is accepted.
The word *pati* is designated as *ghī* only when it occurs in a compound.
patyā,
patye,
patyuḥ
In the word *patyuḥ*, when it occurs before *patau*, the remainder is like that of *hari*.
In a compound, however, when used with "bhūpati," the word *kati* is always plural.
These shall be known as the names of numbers.
A numeral ending in the suffix *ḍati* shall be designated as *ṣaṭ*.
SK 260 / AS 1.1.61: The non-appearance of an affix effected by the words *luk*, *ślu*, and *lup* shall, respectively, receive those specific designations (*luk*, *ślu*, and *lup*).
After the six [case endings], there shall be elision (luk) of the nominative plural suffix *jaś* and the accusative plural suffix *śas*.
Even when a suffix is elided, the grammatical operation dependent upon it should still take place.
Thus, when the rule *jasi ca* (Pāṇini 7.3.109) would require the substitution of the *guṇa* vowel, [the following applies].
The suffixes *luk*, *ślu*, and *lup* are termed *lumat*.
When a suffix marked with *lum* is elided by that [technical] term, the grammatical operation dependent on that [suffix] for the base (*aṅga*) shall not take place—
as in the case of *kati*.
how many,
by how many,
from how many?
From how many, for how many, in how many?
The six terms beginning with *asmad* and *yuṣmad* are identical in form across the three genders;
the word *tri* is always plural and takes the form *trayaḥ*.
three by three from three; three with three; [from] three.
In the presence of the suffix ām, the word *tri* shall undergo the substitution of *traya*.
However, some maintain that [the rule] does not apply when the three [vowels] and the three subsequent [vowels] are secondary (gauṇa).
In reality, however, among the three beloved ones, [the state] belongs to the three beloved ones.
The word *dvi* is always declined in the dual number. (SK 265; Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.92)
The substitute *akāra* (*a*) shall occur for these [words] ending in *dvir*, provided that the rule is intended to apply only to those ending in *dvi* when followed by a case-ending; thus,
*dvau*.
What [is the result] for those ending with two, namely for two and for three?
you (singular), you two (dual),
you (plural)
And because it is a secondary element (*upasarjana*) within a name, the substitution of *n* for *t* does not occur,
since this is an operation belonging to the sub-group beginning with *sarva*; for no one has two names.
Having exceeded two by two, he is "beyond-two" (atidviḥ).
But when [the term] *harivat* signifies preeminence, [the suffix -vat is applied] after words such as *parama*, according to Auḍulomi.
In the case of Auḍulomi, however, in the plural form it becomes uḍulomāḥ;
for it should be stated as a rule (vārttika) that the suffix *akāra* is applied after *loman* when forming the plural of descendants.
An exception to [the suffixes] *bāhv-ādibhyaś ca* (Pāṇini 4.1.96):
*auḍulomi*, *auḍulomī*.
The words ending in "i" include *uḍulomān*;
in the case of *vātapramīḥ*, the suffix *ī* is applied to the root *māṅ* by the *uṇādi* sūtra, and that suffix is *kit*.
He who measures the wind is *vātapramīḥ*;
and [the forms] *vātapramyau* [occur] when there is lengthening before *jas*.
*vātapramyaḥ*— O *vātapramī*, [the form] *vātapramyaḥ* is derived from the base *vātapramī* with the suffix *ami* preceded by [the augment] *pūrvaḥ*. (SK 194)
vātapramīm, vātapramyau, vātapramīn
vātapramyā,
vātapramībhyām, vātapramye.
vātapramyaḥ,
vātapramyoḥ, vātapramyām
Because of the long vowel, the augment *nuṭ* does not occur;
however, in the locative singular (*ṅi*), there is a long vowel by *savarṇa-dīrgha*,
resulting in *vātapramī*.
Among the *vātapramīs*, the same applies to *yayī* and *papī* and so forth;
it is called *yayī* because one goes (*yāti*) by means of it, namely, the path.
The word *papīḥ* (the sun) is derived from the root *pā* (to protect) with the suffix *ī*, according to the rule *sūryaḥ yāpoḥ kid dve ca* (Pāṇini 6.1.115). Thus, the suffix *ī* is applied.

However, there is a distinction for the word *vātapramī*, which ends in the *kvip* suffix, in the cases of the accusative singular (*ami*), the nominative plural (*śasi*), and the locative singular (*ṅau*):
namely, *vātapramyam* and *vātapramyaḥ*.
Regarding the form *bahuśreyasī*: according to the rule to be stated later, "vātapramy-eranekācaḥ" (Pāṇini 6.4.153), the *yaṇ* substitution occurs;
thus, one who has many *śreyasīs* (excellent things) is called *bahuśreyasī*. This is like the word *pradhī*.
Because it ends in a long vowel (dīrghaṅyantatvāt), there is elision of the suffix *su* by Pāṇini 6.1.68 (*halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal*).

Vowels ending in *ī* or *ū* that are invariably feminine are designated as *nadī*. Furthermore, there is a Vārttika stating "and the inclusion of the original gender," which means that even when a word previously denoting a female becomes an *upasarjana* (secondary member of a compound), it should still be declared to retain the *nadī* designation.
In the vocative case, the short vowel [is substituted] for words meaning "mother" (ambārtha) and for those ending in feminine stems denoting rivers (nadī).
He [is] in many blessings,
[possessing] many blessings.
SK 268
AS 7.3.112: After a word ending in "nadī," there shall be the augment āṬ for the following ṅit suffixes.
AS 6.1.90: When *aci* follows, a single substitute *vṛddhi* occurs in place of *āṭ* [and the following vowel]; as in *bahuśreyasyai*.
Because it follows the word *bahuśreyasī*, which ends in a feminine suffix, the augment *nuṭ* is applied [before the genitive plural ending],
resulting in *bahuśreyasīnām*.
After a word ending in *nadī*, after a word ending in *ā*, and after the word *nī*, the suffix *ṅi* shall be replaced by *ām*.
In this case, because it is subsequent, the augment āṬ supersedes the augment nuṬ, as in *bahuśreyasī*;
the remainder is like words ending in the feminine suffix ī, such as *vātapramī*.
Because it ends in a verbal suffix (aṅ), there is no elision of the *su* suffix;
*atilakṣmīḥ* is treated like *bahuśreyasī*.

One who desires a maiden, or a Brāhmaṇa who behaves like a maiden: from the word *kumārī* with the suffix *kyac*, or from the same word with the suffix *ācārakvip*, the suffix *kvip* is applied in the sense of the agent; then, by the rule *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt sutisyapṛktaṃ hal* (Pāṇini 6.1.68), there is elision of the case-ending *su*.

Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.4.77: For a stem ending in the suffix *śnu*, for a verbal root ending in *i* or *u*, and for the stem *bhrū*, the substitutions *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* respectively take place when followed by an affix beginning with a vowel.
The substitute *ṅit* ending is applied;
since *iyaṅ* would otherwise apply to *ī* by the rule "āntaratamyāt" (due to closest similarity), [the rule] "or uvaṅ" results in *iyaṅ*.

and in the alternative, *at* shall replace the *ghī* (the *ī* of the feminine suffix *ṅīp*).
Thus, the Śruti, Smṛti, and so forth, are considered authoritative.
In place of these two [stems] when they are feminine, the substitutes *etad* and *etāv* occur when a case-ending follows.
For the *ṛ* sound of the words *tisṛ* and *catasṛ*, there shall be the substitution of *r*,
which is an exception to [the rules for] *guṇa*, *dīrgha*, and *utva* when followed by a vowel.
The augment *nuṭ* is applied after each of the three [suffixes] beginning with *ām*, provided they follow a stem ending in *num* or a long vowel (*aci*).
In these two cases, there would not be a long vowel for the name.
In the case of "tisṛṇām" and "tisṛṣu," because [the word] "striyām" (in the feminine) is a qualifier for the numbers three and four, it does not apply here.

That which has three or three beloved ones is *priyatri*; like *mati*, there is a distinction in the form *priyatrayām* [in the genitive plural]. However, when the analysis (*vigraha*) is "one who has three beloved women," it is *priyatrisu*.
*priyatisrau*,
*priyatisraḥ*, *priyatisram*, and so forth.

In the case of *priyāstisraḥ* ("one who has three beloveds"), the word *tisṛ* does not undergo the substitution [of *tri*] because the affix is elided (*luk*), and thus the condition for the application of the rule [Pāṇini 1.1.63] is absent. However, since the prohibition [contained in Pāṇini 1.1.63], namely *na lumatāṅgasya*, is considered non-universal (*anitya*) according to some, the form *priyatisṛ* is also possible.
By the rule of prior contradiction (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*), the *num* augment optionally applies before the case-ending substitution:
*priyatisṛṇī* or *priyatisṛṇi*.

In the third case and subsequent cases, due to the optional application of the masculine form (*puṃvadbhāva*) to be described hereafter, there is an alternation between the presence and absence of the *num* augment:
*priyatisrā* and *priyatisṛṇā*.
And so forth;
when there are two *ratva*s, there are two [units]. 2.
From two [comes] 3; of two [comes] 2; Gaurī.
The two white ones [are] the white ones;
[this is] the function of the river.
"Gaurī, Gauryai," and so forth;
likewise for Vāṇī, Nādī, and the others.

Since the mention of a nominal stem includes its gender-qualified form as well, both the substitution of *anaṅ* and the treatment as having a *ṇit* suffix would apply; however, by the maxim "in the mention of a nominal stem, the gender-qualified form is not included" (*prātipadikagrahaṇe liṅgaviśiṣṭasyāgrahaṇam*), [the substitution does not apply] before a case-ending— thus, [the form is] *sakhī*.
"Sakhyau," "sakhyaḥ," and so forth, are like [the declension of] Gaurī.
Because it ends in an *aṅ* suffix, there is no elision of the *su* case-ending; *lakṣmīḥ* is declined like *gaurī*.
In this way, words such as *tarītavyā* (to be crossed) and others ending in feminine suffixes take the vocative singular form *he stri*.
In the case of the word *strī*, the substitution *iyaṅ* occurs when followed by an affix beginning with a vowel.
Two women; women.
In the feminine, before the suffixes *ami* and *śas*, *iyaṅ* optionally replaces [the final vowel] of a word denoting a woman.
strī, striyau, striyaḥ

striyāḥ, striyāḥ, striyoḥ
The augment *nuṭ* is applied after [the word] *strī* when it occurs in the feminine gender due to its being subsequent [in the rule].
One who has surpassed women among women is *atistriḥ*.

It should be understood that for the word *strī*, the substitution *iyaṅ* is superseded by the addition of the augment *num* in the neuter, and in the masculine, it is superseded by the addition of the suffixes *guṇa*, *nābhāva*, *ut*, and *anuṭ*, due to their higher priority in the order of application.
And in the case of *jasi*,
[the form is] *atistriyaḥ*; [in the case of *he* (vocative singular), it is] *he atistre*.
*he atistriyau*, *he atistrayaḥ* [are the forms] in the *vāmśas* (instrumental and following) cases. (SK Sandarbha 302)
atistriyam, atistrim, atistriyau
atistriyaḥ, atistrīn, atistriṇā
In the case of *gher*, [the substitution of *āT* occurs] before a word ending in *ṅi* (locative singular) and before *atistri*. Thus:
*atistriye*, *atistreḥ*.
atistreḥ, atistriyoḥ, atistrīṇām; atistriyāḥ, atistriyoḥ, atistrīṇām; atistriyām, atistriyoḥ, atistrīṣu.
The substitution of *at* for the final vowel and the following consonant of the word *strī* occurs before a case-ending beginning with a vowel, except in the locative singular (*strau*).
Thus, *ati-strī*.

The substitution of *iy* occurs invariably before the suffix *os* and optionally before the suffixes *am* and *śas*; however, this substitution of *iy* takes place before a vowel-ending case-suffix and not elsewhere. In the masculine, when [the word] is a subordinate member (*upasarjana*), the substitution does not occur; but in the neuter, the augment *num* is added.
atistri, atistriṇī, atistrīṇi
In the case of *atistri*,
before endings beginning with *ṅe* and so forth that start with vowels— where the previously mentioned rule for masculine-like behavior (*puṃvadbhāva*) optionally applies— the form is as before.
atistraye, atistriṇaḥ, atistriṇaḥ
atistreḥ, atistreḥ, atistriṇoḥ
*atistriṇoḥ*,
*atistriyoḥ*, and so forth; however, in the feminine, it is generally like the masculine.

In the case of *śas* (the accusative plural ending), the optional application [of the feminine suffix *āP*] is triggered by the fact that the stem ends in a short vowel, according to the rule *atistriyāḥ* and *hrasvaśca* when followed by a *ṅit* affix.
However, the word *astrī* is a *paryudāsa* (exclusion) specifically of the rule *iyaṅuvaṅsthānau*;
because it follows only that which is connected to it, this prohibition applies to the long vowel and not to the short one, as in *atistriyai*.
atistriye, atistriyāḥ,
atistriyāḥ
Of each one who has transgressed, of each one who has transgressed, of those who have transgressed excessively.

According to Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 1.4.4, those long vowels *ī* and *ū* which possess the substitutes *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* do not receive the designation *nadī*; however, this does not apply to the word *strī*, as in the example:
"O Śrī! (*he śrīḥ*).

The two vowels *i* and *u*, when they are substitutes for *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* and are designated as feminine (*strī-ākhyau*), optionally bear the technical name *nadī* before the case-ending *āmi*; however, this does not apply to the words *strī* and *śrī*, as in the forms *strīṇām* and *śriyām*.
In the glories of glories, in the glory of glories.

Regarding the word *pradhī*, however, according to the opinion of the Vṛttikāra and others, its form is like that of *lakṣmī*; since it is accepted that its status as a "constant feminine" (*nityastrītva*) consists in its denoting a female even without another word, it does not denote other genders. But in Kaiyaṭa’s opinion, its form is like that of the masculine.

In the analysis *prakṛṣṭā dhīḥ* ("excellent intellect"), the forms are *pradhyaṃ* and *pradhya* in the accusative singular due to the suffix *ami* and *śasi*, with the specific change [of *dhī-* to *dhy-]* as in *lakṣmī*. However, in the analysis *suṣṭhu dhīryasyāḥ* ("she whose intellect is excellent") or *suṣṭhu dhyāyati* ("she who meditates well"), the form is *sudhīḥ* according to the rule for compound formation, just like *śrīḥ*.
According to another opinion, however, in the analysis *suṣṭhu dhīḥ* (a very wise woman), the form is like *śrī*, and likewise [in the case of] *grāmaṇīḥ*, it is *puṃvat*.
Since leading a village is generally a duty of men and does not apply to women in the absence of other scriptural indications,

Many scholars maintain that this is simply a lapse;
however, the word *khalapūḥ* (a sweeper) is treated as masculine.
In the case of *punarbhū*,
because the *yaṇ* [substitution] subverts the *uvaṅ* [substitution], the prohibition stated in Pāṇini 7.1.82 (*neyaṅuvaṅsthānāv astrī*) does not apply; thus,
one says *he punarbho*.
punarbhvam,
punarbhvau, punarbhvaḥ

In a compound whose final member consists of a single vowel (ekāc), there shall be obligatory *ṇatva* for the *n* of a nominal stem ending (*pratipadikānta*), of the suffixes *num*, *vi*, or *bha*, or of one situated within a suffix (*pratyayastha*), provided that it follows a cause (*nimitta*) located in the preceding member (*pūrvapada*).

Since permanence is established by the force of the initial statement (*ārambhasāmarthya*), the repetition of the letter *ṇ* is for the sake of clarity; it serves to override the *yaṇ* substitution and, by virtue of its higher status (*paratva*), ensures that *nuṭ* occurs again for the words beginning with *punar*, *bhū*, and *nau*.
*Varṣābhūḥ* refers to the species of frog; because it lacks permanent femininity, one says *he varṣābhūḥ* according to Kaiyaṭa’s view,
but in another opinion, *he varṣābhu*.
Regarding *punarnavā*, however, [the forms] are *varṣābhū* (feminine) and *bhekyāṃ* (feminine);
Yādava states that *punarnavā* is feminine, while *varṣābhū* is masculine when referring to a frog;
thus, the dual form is *varṣābhvau*.
*Varṣābhvaḥ* and *svayambhūḥ* are treated like masculine nouns. (SK 308)
The suffixes *ṅīp* and *ṭāp* do not occur after those [stems] designated as "ṣat" nor after *svasṛ* and the others;
namely, *svasṛ*, *tisṛ*, *catasṛ*, *nanāndṛ*, and likewise *duhitṛ*.
"Yātā," "mātā"— these seven, beginning with *svasṛ*, have been cited;
by the rule *aptṛn* (Pāṇini 6.4.11), there is lengthening,

The sound *śi* shall have the technical designation [“place of articulation”] as previously stated.

AS 7.1.72: The augment *num* is added to a neuter stem ending in a *jhal* consonant or a vowel, when a *sarvanāmasthāna* suffix follows; furthermore, there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhādīrghaḥ*).
The cognitions, moreover, are like that; the remainder is as in the case of Rāma.

Because the fifth case-ending (*ṭi*) has been elided, there is neither the substitution of the homogeneous long vowel (*pūrvasavarṇadīrgha*) by Pāṇini 6.1.102, nor the elision of the vocative suffix (*saṃbuddhilopa*) by Pāṇini 6.1.68.

When one or the other [of the two *s* sounds] is replaced by *ś*, then due to the *saṃnipāta-paribhāṣā* rule, there is no substitution of *jaras* in the case of *ajaram*.
In *ajara-si*,
because it is *ajara* (ending in a vowel), when *si* is applied, the augment *num* is added because it ends in a *jhal* consonant.

When a *sarvanāmasthāna* other than the vocative singular follows, there shall be lengthening of the penultimate vowel of a word ending in *n*, provided that the *n* is preceded by a conjunct consonant (*saṃyoga*) or is part of the word *mahat*.

*hṛdi*, *hṛdā*, *hṛdbhyām*, and so forth.

because [the compound] is a *bha*-stem by virtue of being included in the *ayasmaya-ādi* group, there is no elision of the final consonant of the *saṃyoga*.

For although the term *chandasi* (in Vedic) is carried over [from the previous rule] in the commentary on *paddanna* (Pāṇini 6.1.63), nevertheless, according to the method stated by Kaiyaṭa—that because of the explicit mention of *chandas* in the Vārttika *apobhi* (Pāṇini 7.1.35) "māsaśchandasī," [the substitution of *pad* for *mās*] occurs even in the worldly (*laukika*) usage in certain instances—one should understand that words such as *pada* and others are to be employed in accordance with actual usage.
In the neuter gender, there shall be a short vowel for a nominal stem ending in /ā/; for example,
*śrīpam*,
which is like *jñānam*.

After a neuter stem ending in /a/, there shall be elision (*luk*) of the suffixes *su* and *am*; for example, *vāri*.
According to Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.1.73, the augment *num* is added to a neuter stem ending in an *ik* vowel when followed by a case-ending beginning with a vowel.
Because the prohibition "vāriṇī vārīṇi na lumatā" (Pāṇini 1.1.63) is not universal, the *guṇa* substitution caused by the vocative case occurs optionally.
He vāre! He vāri āṅo nā. (Pāṇini 6.1.94) [SKsandarbhaḥ 244]

When *guṇa* would otherwise be obtained by the rule *vāriṇā gher ṅiti*, [the form *vāriṇā* is established] by the prior application (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*) of *num* over *vṛddhi*, *auttva*, *tṛjvadbhāva*, and *guṇa*.

By the rule *numacireti nuṭ* (Pāṇini 6.4.3) and *nāmī* (Pāṇini 6.4.3), a long vowel is substituted [for the penultimate short vowel], resulting in *vārīṇām*.
In the case of *vāri* followed by *vārin-* with an initial consonant, it is like *hari*.

When the cause for application [of the gender] is identical, a neuter word ending in the vowel *i* that has been mentioned as masculine may optionally take the masculine form before a suffix beginning with a vowel other than *ṭ*.

to the one without beginning,
and so forth.

For these [stems ending in *an*], *aṅ* shall be substituted before suffixes beginning with *ṭ* and vowels; and that [substitute] is acute.

by the application of the *num* augment through a prior counter-exception (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*) to the rule for the *tṛjvat* substitution,

In the case where [the feminine] is treated like the masculine (*puṃvat*) before suffixes beginning with *ṭa*, [the forms are]: *priyakroṣṭrā*,
*priyakroṣṭunā*, *priyakroṣṭre*.
In the case of *priyakroṣṭave*, by a prior counter-exception (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*) to the substitution of a *tṛjvat* stem, only the *num* augment applies,
resulting in *priyakroṣṭunā*.

When short vowels are being prescribed, *ec* (e, o, ai, au) shall be replaced by *ig* (i, u, ṛ, ḷ) only; for example, *pradyu*.
*Pradyunī*, *pradyūni*, *pradyune*, and so forth.

Therefore, [the rule] "kvip" should not apply here in the case of *dāmaliṭ*.

In place of *baś* (the consonants *b*, *bh*, *g*, *gh*, *j*, *jh*, *d*, *dh*, *d*, *dh*, *v*) which is a part of a verbal root (*dhātu*) that has a single vowel (*ekāj*) and ends in a *jhaṣ* (the consonants *j*, *jh*, *b*, *bh*, *g*, *gh*, *d*, *dh*, *d*, *dh*, *v*), there shall be *bhaṣ* (the consonants *bh*, *gh*, *jh*, *dh*, *dh*, *v*) when followed by the letter *s*, the word *dhva*, or at the end of a word (*padānta*).
If the rule were construed with grammatical coreferentiality (*sāmānādhikaraṇya*) as "of a one-vowel root," then it would not apply here [in cases where the root is part of a larger complex].

In *śasi priyāṣṭnaḥ*, even though the elision (*al-lopa*) occurs by rule before the preceding [suffix], there is no substitution of *ṣ* for *s* either because of the status of that elision as *sthānivadbhāva* (as if it were the original element), or else, according to the *kāryakāla* view, because the external *al-lopa* is considered *asiddha* (non-existent) for the purpose of the internal operation.

In the rule *priyāṣṭā* and so forth, the substitution of *āt* for the nominative-accusative dual endings (*jaś* and *śas*) is inferred; this occurs only when [the word *aṣṭan*] is primary (*prādhānya*), and not when it is secondary (*gauṇatā*).
Consequently, the optional substitution of *āt* applies to *priyāṣṭan* only before consonant-initial endings (*halādi*).

like *rājā*, there is elision (*vatsarga*) [of the *n*], and in the case of the locative plural ending *hal*,

AS 7.2.94: In the presence of the nominative singular suffix *su*, the substitutes *tva* and *aha* take the place of the non-final portions of *yuṣmad* and *asmad* respectively.

When a case-ending other than those that cause the substitution of *ā* or *yat* follows, there is elision of the final phoneme of *yuṣmad* and *asmad*. [This is followed by] Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.97: Before the ending *am*, the preceding vowel and the following vowel coalesce into a single substitute (pūrvarūpa).

In the case of *tvaṃ aham* and *nanu tvaṃ strī ahaṃ strī*, where *tvam a am* and *aham a am* have been established, the substitution of the prior form (*ami pūrvarūpam*) is set aside by the application of the feminine suffix *ṭāp*, because it is an *antaraṅga* (internal) operation.
The words *yuṣmad* and *asmad* are neuter and lack a gender marker;
therefore, because they lack femininity, the suffix *ṭāp* does not apply.

Alternatively, the term "śeṣa" is used in the locative case to express the locus (*adhikaraṇa*) of the original element (*sthānin*); thus, there is the elision of the *ad* following that which ends in *map*,
and this elision takes effect even though it is subsequent, once the internal rule *ato guṇe* has been applied.
Therefore, because it lacks the property of ending in a short vowel (adanta), the suffix *ṭāp* does not apply; thus, [the form] is *paramāham*.

"the devotee meditates on your form" (*dhyāyati*), whereas in the case of direct perception, it is "the devotee sees you with his eyes" (*paśyati*).
When these two [pronouns] follow a word ending in the nominative case that has already appeared previously, these substitutions shall occur even in the case of subsequent reference (anvādeśa).
"You are my devotee and I am his; therefore, Hari protects you and he protects me—or rather, he protects both you and me.
That which ends in the nominative case when used in address shall be designated as *āmantrita* (vocative).
O Agni, it is clear that [this] is yours.
O gods, protect us; O Agni, lead us; O Agni, Indra, Varuṇa.
In this context, the substitutes for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* [retain their accent], as do the *tiṅ*-endings (*tiṅ-nighāta*) and vocatives (*āmantrita-nighāta*).
However, in the phrase *rakṣa deva naḥ*, although the word *deva* is treated as if non-existent (*avidyamānavat*), the substitute [for *naḥ*] occurs by relying on the preceding word *rakṣa*.

Similarly, in the mantra *imaṃ me gaṅge yamune*, although the vocatives preceding *yamune* and the others are treated as if non-existent, the *nighāta* (anudātta accent) of all [the preceding words] occurs by relying solely on the word *me*.
A qualificand (*viśeṣya*) followed by a vocative (*āmantrita*) in grammatical apposition (*samānādhikaraṇa*) shall not be treated as non-existent (*avidyamānavat*).
"O Hari, O Compassionate One, protect us!

[This occurs] in the context of a specific statement (*viśeṣavacana*). Regarding this, the Bhāṣya says: "I shall state that it is the plural number."
When a plural-ending substantive is followed by a vocative adjective in grammatical apposition, it may optionally be treated as if it were present; for example:
"O you who are powerful, O gods who are our refuge! (yūyaṃ prabhavo devāḥ śaraṇyāḥ).
"I worship you, O gods; I worship you who are worthy of refuge. Or: "I worship you, O gods; I worship you who are worthy of refuge."
In this case, even in the context of an anvādeśa (subsequent reference), the optional substitutes are *supāt* or *supād*.
One with beautiful feet [should bow] to one with beautiful feet, or to one with beautiful feet.
The word *supāda-* [is used as a Bahuvrīhi compound] when it denotes a person who possesses beautiful feet;
Pāṇini Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.4.130.

"Supadbhyām" and so forth;

There is elision of the *n* of stems ending in a consonant that do not have *i* as an *it*, before an affix marked with *k* or *ṅ*. By the rule *ugidacām* (Pāṇini 7.1.70), the *num* augment is added;
then, by the rule *saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.23), the final consonant cluster is elided.
By the rule *numo nakārasya kvinpratyayasya kuḥ* (Pāṇini 8.2.62), the letter *ṅ* [of *ṅvan*] becomes *k*; then,
through the rules for *anusvāra* and *parasavarṇa*, it becomes *m*.

There shall be elision of the vowel *a* belonging to the element *añc*, which is a *bha*-stem, when the letter *n* has been elided.

as in *prācaḥ* and *prācā*.
"From the two eastern ones," and so forth; "pratyaṅ" means "the two western ones."

In the case of the elision [of the final vowel] by the rule *acaḥ*, the *yaṇ* substitution does not apply— even though it is an internal (*antaraṅga*) operation— due to the metarule *akṛtavyūhāḥ*. Thus,
[the form is] *pratīcaḥ*.
In the analysis of the compound *pratyañc* as "that which goes toward that" (*amum añcati*), the form *adas-añc* remains [prior to further derivation].
For these two [words] and for a pronoun, the substitution of *adri* for the final *ṭi* occurs when followed by the suffix *añcu* ending in a non-pratyaya (*apratyaya*).
When *adadri-añca* is thus established, the *yaṇ* [substitution] applies.
In the word *adas*, when it does not end in *as*, the vowels *u* and *ū* are substituted for the vowel following the *d*, and *m* is substituted for the *d*.

The term *u* is a collective dvandva compound of the short (*hrasva*) and long (*dīrgha*) vowels; by the principle of closest proximity (*āntaratamya*), the short vowel [substitutes] for both the short vowel and the consonant, while the long vowel [substitutes] for the long vowel— as in the example *amumuyaṅ*.

In forms such as *amumuyagbhyām*, because the substitution of *m* (*mutva*) is considered *asiddha*, the *yaṇ* replacement does not occur.

According to the view of those who rely on the paribhāṣā "when the final [element] is barred, that which is in the vicinity of the final [element] is affected," they maintain that the *mutva* applies only to the subsequent [element], resulting in *adamuyaṅ*.

Regarding the word *asi* (the nominative singular of *adas*), because it is explained as "that which has *s* in place of [the final letter]," the substitution of *m* (*mutva*) applies only in the domain of the *tyadādi* (pronominal) *atva* change and not elsewhere; this is the position stated in the *adadyaṅ*: "Some desire the *mutva* of *adas* to be distinct from the *adreḥ* (the *adr-* portion), like the *latva* [of *lat*];
some [hold that it applies] to the final homogeneous segment (*antyasadeśa*), while one [holds] 'no'—for it is seen in *asi*."

Therefore, by the rule *kṛkami* (Pāṇini 8.3.46),

*avadattam*, *ahayuḥ*, *astikṣīrā*, *a*, *ā*, *i*, *ī*, *u*, *ū*, *e*, *ai*, *o*, *au*, *paśu*, *śukam*, *yathākathāca*, *pāṭ*, *pyāṭ*, *aṅga*, *hai*, *he*, *bhoḥ*, *aye*, *dya*, *viṣu*, *ekapade*, *yut*, *ātaḥ*; this class beginning with *ca* (the *cādi* group) is also an open-ended class (*ākṛtigaṇa*).
That [nominal stem] from which no case-ending (vibhakti) arises shall be an indeclinable (avyaya), provided it ends in a secondary suffix (taddhita).
An enumeration must be made:
[the suffixes] beginning with *tasil* up to *pāśap*, and those beginning with *śas* up to the compound-final suffixes (*samāsānta*).
Having made "ām" and "ām," the purposes [are accomplished].
Because it is not various, it is not [present] here.
Almost a cooked state, almost a form of cooking.
SK 449
A word ending in a *kṛt* suffix that ends in *m*, as well as a word ending in the suffix *ej*, shall be indeclinable (*avyaya*). For example: *smāram smāram*.
To live,
to drink.
Up to this point (AS 1-1-40), it should be understood as an indeclinable (*avyaya*) after having performed [the action].
The one who has risen up and spread forth.
SK 451
adhihari (with regard to Hari) AS 1.1.41;
There is elision (luk) of the case-ending *ap* and of the *sup* suffixes prescribed after an indeclinable (*avyaya*), as in the word *tatra śālāyām*.

In this case, because the qualifier has been applied [to the whole], even though there is the rule of "extension to what ends with that" (*tadantavidhi*) regarding the designation of an indeclinable (*avyaya*), nevertheless it does not apply to a secondary (*gauṇa*) sense.
The inclusion of the term "ā" is redundant because [the definition] lacks a gender marker.
(Vārttika: That which remains unchanged—similar across the three genders, all case-endings, and all numbers—is called *avyaya* (indeclinable).
Thus, the Vedic scripture cited in the Bhāṣya intends to convey the absence of gender, number, and case-role; for Bhāguri maintains that there is elision of the *a* of the prefixes *ava* and *api*,
as well as of the *āp* of words ending in *āp*, just as in the cases of *vācā*, *niśā*, and *diśā*.
Immersion, plunging, and covering.
"Apidhānam" concludes the section on indeclinables;
now begins the section on feminine suffixes.
This is a heading.
"Of those that are capable," so much is meant. (SK 454; AS 4-1-4)

The suffix *ṭāp* shall be applied when femininity is to be expressed for words beginning with vowels other than *a*, as well as for words ending in *a*; the mention of "beginning with *a*" (*ajādi*) is for the purpose of setting aside the application of *ṅīṣ* and *ṅīp*. Example:
*ajā*.
Therefore— because [the word] *khaṭvā* is qualified by *ajā* and so forth as feminine, there is no formation of *pañcājī* here.

By the rule *dvigoḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.21), the suffix *ṅīp* is applied here; for in this case, the feminine gender resides in the collective sense (*samāhāra*) which constitutes the meaning of the compound, as in the word *ajā*.
A ewe, a mare, and a sparrow.
In these [words] such as *mūṣikā*, the suffix *ṅīṣ* is obtained by virtue of the characteristic of the genus (*jāti*),
as in the case of *bālā*.
Vatsā,
Hoḍā, and Mandā.

The suffix *ṅīp* is applicable [after the word *vilātā*] when it occurs in the first stage of life, according to the rule "in these [words ending in short *a*, the suffix *ṅīp* is applied] in the first age" (*SKSandarbha* 478); however, [the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied] after *sambhastṛ*, *ajina*, *śaṇa*, *piṇḍa*, and *phala*.
In the word *saṃphalā*, the short vowel is substituted [for the long vowel] by the rule *bhastraphalāṅgyāpoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.159).
From hundreds of excellent stalks and tips of flowers,
she is the one with true flowers,
the one who has flowers from of old.
A *śūdrā* who has not previously been married to a man of higher caste is [called] *pratyakpuṣpā* by birth; however, when she is in union with a man [of higher caste], she is called *śūdrī*.
Why [is it specified] "not preceded by *mahat*"? [Consider: *mahāśūdrī*, *kruñcā*, *uṣṇihā*.
The divine clans, the eldest and the youngest.

The word *madhyamā* [is formed with the suffix ṅīṣ] when expressing a relationship with a male (*puṃyoga*), and also when expressing a genus (*jāti*) provided it does not originate from the negative particle *nañ*. (Vārttika)
The suffix *ṅīp* is applied after words ending in *ṛn* that do not have a root as their base; for example, *kartrī*.
The staff-bearer (daṇḍinī) [is formed according to] Pāṇini’s *Sūtra* 4.1.6.
The suffix *ṅīp* shall be applied in the feminine after a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) ending in an *ugit* vowel; for example: *pacantī*, *bhavantī*.

By the inclusion of the term *aj* (vowel) in the rule *ugidacām* (Pāṇini 7.1.70), which prescribes the augment *num*, it is restricted that if a vowel-initial root is to undergo an operation conditioned by the *ugit* designation, then it must be the root *añc* alone. This is illustrated by the form *dīvyantī* from the root *śap* (in the sense of cursing).
Therefore, the suffix *kvip* does not occur here after the root *ukh-sṛ*.
By the rule *aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti* (Pāṇini 6.4.24), there is elision of the *n* in *parṇadhvat*;
however, for the root *añc*, it would indeed occur.
East and west.
After a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) ending in *van*, or one that ends in such a stem, the suffix *ṅīp* shall occur in the feminine, and *ra* shall be the substitute for the final [phoneme].
The term *van* is a general designation for the suffixes *ṅvanip*, *kvanip*, and *vanip*.
When a suffix is mentioned, there is the inclusion of that which begins with the element after which it is prescribed and ends with it;

therefore, because the suffix qualifies the nominal stem (*prātipadika*), even that which ends in what ends in it is obtained— as in *atisutvarī*, meaning "one who has surpassed those who have performed the *sū* sacrifice."
The night is exceedingly dark;
it should be said, "Like a forest, it is not visible. (Or: "It is as if a forest were not visible.")

The meaning is that the suffix *ṅīp* and *raś* are not applied after a nominal stem (*prātipadika*) ending in *van*, nor after one ending in a *van* that is prescribed after a root (*dhātu*) having *ha* as its penultimate letter. [For example:
from the root *oṇṛ* (in the sense of "removing"), the suffix *vanip* is applied.
By the rule *viḍvanoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.41), there is the substitution of *ā* for *ava*; thus,
*brāhmaṇī rājayudhvā*.
In a bahuvrīhi compound, optionally:
*bahudhīvarī* or *bahudhīvā*.
In this context, the suffix *ḍāp* will be explained [in Sūtra 4.1.8].
The word *pād* has the suffix *samāsānta* [–a] applied; from that nominal stem ending in it, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* may optionally occur:
*dvipadī* or *dvipāt*.
When *ṛc* is to be expressed, the suffix *ṭāp* shall be applied after the final syllable of a quarter-verse (*pāda*).
A *ṛc* consisting of two feet or one foot [is not shortened], nor [is it shortened] after words such as *ṣaṭ*, *svasṛ*, and so forth. (Pāṇini 6.1.172–174)

In the case of *pañcacatasaḥ* and *pañca*, even though the elision of *n* (*nalopa*) has occurred, the designation *ṣaṭ* (six) still applies according to the rule *ṣṇāntā ṣaṭ* (Pāṇini 1.1.24). This is because the elision of *n* is considered non-existent (*asiddha*) for the purposes of the rules regarding case endings (*sup*) and accents (*svara*), as per the rule *nalopaḥ supsvarasaṃjñātugvidhiṣu* (Pāṇini 8.2.2). Consequently, the feminine suffix *ṭāp* is not applied by the rule *na ṣaṭsvasrādibhyaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.1.10).
The suffix *ṅīp* is not applied after a word ending in the masculine suffix *man*.
sīmā, sīmānau (SK 460)
The suffix *ṅīp* is not applied after a *bahuvrīhi* compound ending in *anna*; for example, *bahuyajvā*.
The two performers of many sacrifices (bahuyajvānau).
After the two vowels [i and u] included in the two sūtras, the suffix ḍāp may optionally be applied; thus,
*sīmā* or *sīme*.
The two temples are the two cords; the two cords are the two temples.
According to Amara, the word *dāmā* is used in the masculine as *dāmānau*, while *dāmā* is used in the singular; [he was] one who had performed many sacrifices (*bahuyajvā*).
*bahuyajvan* (masculine singular nominative), *bahuyajvānau* (masculine dual nominative) SK 462.

After a Bahuvrīhi compound ending in *anna*, the suffix *ṅīp* may optionally be applied when the penultimate vowel is elided; alternatively, in that case, there is the option of the suffix *ḍāp* or the prohibition [of both].
bahurājñī, bahurājñau, bahurāje
The two words *bahu* and *rājānau* [form a compound] according to Pāṇini 2.4.62.
When the suffix *āp* follows, an *i* should replace the vowel *a* preceding the letter *ka*, provided that this *āp* does not follow a *sup* (nominal) suffix;
as in *sarvikā* and *kārikā*.
What follows from this? [The rule applies] after a suffix ending in "kim. [Example: *śakā* (from *śaknoti*). Why "not after a word ending in a sup-suffix"? [Counter-example: *bahuparivrājakā nagarī*.
Why "kāṭ"? [It is] for the sake of the former; why "nandanā"? So that it may not be "kaṭukā" for the latter.
Why [is it] "followed by *t*"? [Consider: *rākā*.
Why [is it] "*api*"? [Consider: *kārakaḥ*.
There should be an addition [to the rule] regarding *māmaka* and *narakayaḥ*. (Vārttika)
The word *narikā* means "one who makes men her own" (*māmikān narān kāyati*); [this is derived from the root] *kai* with the suffix *ṇvul*, and the long vowel is optionally shortened.
The woman from the south and the woman from here,
In the case of *yat*, *tat*, and *daḥ*, when followed by *asya*, the suffix *yaK* shall not occur.
One's own desire and that which is desired.
And there is a prohibition against dropping [the final vowel] (or):
*adhityakā*,
*upatyakā*.
In the sense of a blessing, the suffix *vun* is optionally absent;
thus [the forms] *jīvakā* and *bhavakā*.
And when there is elision of the final member [of a compound], [the suffix *ka* is optionally applied]: *devadattikā*, *devakā*.
And for words such as *kṣipakā*, [the feminine suffix] *kā* is optionally used; thus,
[the forms] *kṣipakā* and *dhruvakā*.
*kanyā*, *caṭakā*, and *tārakā* [are used] in the sense of "star" (*jyotis*).
Except for a weaver’s shuttle, there is no other colored thread in the weaving;
except for the colored thread, there is nothing else.
The word *vartakā* refers to a bird among the Easterners, while for the Northerners it is *vartikā*;
*aṣṭakā* refers to the ancestral deities (*pitṛdaivatyā*).
It should be stated that [the vowel *a*] optionally occurs after the words *aṣṭikā*, *nyā*, *sūtakā*, *putrikā*, and *vṛndāraka*; or rather, the division here is *vā a*.
The meaning is that there is an optional substitution of *a* for the vowel preceding *k*;

thus, in the word *putrikā*, in the alternative case, *a* is substituted for the *i*-vowel of the suffix *ṅīn*. In other instances, however, it is specifically *a* that is optionally substituted for *a* in order to preclude the application of *itva*.
"Sūtakā, sūtikā," and so forth (SK 465).

According to Pāṇini’s Aṣṭādhyāyī 7.3.46, for that vowel *a* which stands in place of the feminine suffix *ā* preceded by *ya*, there is optionally the substitution of *it* (i.e., *i*) when followed by the suffix *āp*, provided it is preceded by *ka*; furthermore, by Pāṇini’s Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.97 (*ke’ṇaḥ*), the short vowel is substituted [for the long *ā*].
The noble man and the noble woman, the little sparrows.
"Caṭakikā"—what is the meaning? "Sāṃkāśyikā," meaning one who comes from Sāṃkāśya;
why [is it] "yak"? [Answer: "Aśvikā."
What is the purpose of the condition "before a feminine suffix"? [Consider: *śubham yāti* ("she goes auspiciously") = *śubhaṃyāḥ*.
When it is unknown (*ajñātā*), it becomes *śubhaṃyāḥ* or *śubhaṃyikā*.
However, [the suffix] *yaK* at the end of a verbal root is always [subject to this rule]. (Vārttika)
She who is a skilled cook and a skillful baker.
The word ending in *sva*, with its genitive case marker elided, is a term for these [suffixes]; the vowel *i* may optionally replace the final vowel of such a word.
